size.note: Wikipedia gives 11 cm. Newman's Birds gives 12–13 cm.

habitat: Open savanna and short grassland with bare ground, including recently burnt ground, fallow fields, road verges and airstrips, often on reddish soils.
summary: A small, strongly patterned sparrow-lark. The male is black on the head and underparts, with white patches on the nape and behind the eye, and chestnut upperparts. The female is streaked buff-white on the head and underparts, with a thin whitish collar, a dark belly patch, and mottled chestnut upperparts. Young birds are like the female. Both sexes have grey underwings. Chick down is not described.

similar.note: Grey-backed Sparrow-Lark has a grey back. Its male has a small white cap. Female Chestnut-backed Sparrow-Lark is darker above, with reddish wing coverts and bolder breast streaks.
Red-capped Lark has a rufous cap and rufous breast-side patches on pale underparts, and the sexes look alike.

viewNotes.note: Chestnut wing coverts. The bird makes off low and irregularly, then resettles.
Both sexes have grey underwings, which separates them from the other sparrow-larks in Newman’s account.
The male’s face and breast are black, with a white patch behind the eye. The female’s face is streaked buff-white.
Chestnut upperparts. The male’s white nape patch and the female’s thin whitish collar show from behind.
Male: black underparts, white cheek patch and chestnut back. Female: streaked buff underparts, a dark belly spot and chestnut coverts.
Young birds are like the female. A separate chick colour is not described.

calls.description: A sharp rattling chip-chwep; the texts used here do not assign it to one sex.
A pretty song given in fluttering flight; the texts used here do not transcribe it or assign it to one sex.

research.note: Kemp classed it as a visiting breeder. Newman calls it a resident, and SABAP1 says it is resident in some areas and nomadic in the Transvaal, with records in every season. All twelve months are listed. A female photograph and a flight photograph were not found in the open Kruger set used here. Both grade A recordings are from outside southern Africa; no higher-grade southern African file was available. The iNaturalist account name on the second photograph is maritzasouthafrica. Chick down is not described.
